review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment read including title and deck; complete existing English retained, fifteen localized corrections awaiting independent second review. Stalemate retained after checking its explicit definition in units 78–83.

changes.before: Each form carries its own temptation. And all three temptations point at the same thing — freezing some wartime state into a new permanent one, so that cultivation still cannot come back afterward.
changes.after: Each form carries its own temptation. And all three temptations point at the same thing — freezing some wartime state into a new long-term one, so that cultivation still cannot come back afterward.
changes.reason: Long-term is not necessarily permanent; preserve 长期.

changes.before: The cannot-not that justified starting has been dissolved by the war. At the same time, the other side still exists as a carrier of cultivation. And the victor has not, in the process, become a new suppressive structure itself.
changes.after: The cannot-not that justified starting has been dissolved by the war. At the same time, the other side still exists as a subject of cultivation. And the victor has not, in the process, become a new suppressive structure itself.
changes.reason: Restore 主体 rather than substituting the distinct term carrier.

changes.before: So the firewall states correctly as: do not colonize, but keep watching.
changes.after: So the firewall is correctly stated as: do not colonize, but keep watching.
changes.reason: Repair English grammar while retaining the injunction. The Chinese seven-character claim is eight characters and is not imported as an English claim.

changes.before: No causal claim is being made here. The origins of a war are always more complicated than any single treaty, and hanging what happened twenty years later on 1919 is dishonest history. The observation is structural only: on the question of whether the defeated side remains in the system as a subject, the two settlements ran in opposite directions. And that question is precisely the line the firewall draws.
changes.after: No causal claim is being made here. The origins of a war are always more complicated than any single treaty, and simply hanging what happened twenty years later on 1919 is dishonest history. The observation is structural only: on the question of whether the defeated side remains in the system as a subject, the two settlements ran in opposite directions. And that question is precisely the line the firewall draws.
changes.reason: Restore 简单: the source rejects reductive attribution, not any causal connection.

changes.before: Nearly every other framework's war thought endorses collective self-annihilation in some situation — when defeat is irreversible and submission unacceptable, going down to the last is treated as the dignified choice. The Chinese phrase is "better a shattered jade than an intact tile," and versions of it recur across civilizations, always carrying tragedy, honor, and the dignity of at least not having yielded.
changes.after: Nearly every other framework's war thought endorses collective self-annihilation in some situation — when defeat is irreversible and humiliation unacceptable, going down to the last is treated as the dignified choice. The Chinese phrase is "better a shattered jade than an intact tile," and versions of it recur across civilizations, always carrying tragedy, honor, and the dignity of at least not having yielded.
changes.reason: Restore 屈辱 without collapsing it into yielding/submission.

changes.before: A final observation: self-annihilation becomes a stable, visible option only when both sides are locked in the same vocabulary. The pressed side understands its situation in the language of honor and defeat, so going down looks dignified as the end approaches; the pressing side treats the other as an enemy rather than as a subject who has not yet stood up, so it drives the other into a corner and leaves no room for continuing as a subject. Only when the two vocabularies interlock does the option take shape.
changes.after: A final observation: self-annihilation becomes a stable, visible option only when both sides are locked in the same vocabulary. The pressed side understands its situation in the language of honor and winning or losing, so going down looks dignified as the end approaches; the pressing side treats the other as an enemy rather than as a subject who has not yet stood up, so it drives the other into a corner and leaves no room for continuing as a subject. Only when the two vocabularies interlock does the option take shape.
changes.reason: Restore both halves of 胜负, not only defeat.

changes.before: They want gains — trade gains for time. The mildest situation. They want resources, territory, trade rights, tribute, a posture of submission. They are not pursuing your disappearance as a subject.
changes.after: They want gains — trade gains for time. The mildest situation. They want resources, territory, trade rights, tax revenue, a posture of submission. They are not pursuing your disappearance as a subject.
changes.reason: Restore 税收; tribute is a narrower and different category.

changes.before: The response is to concede at the level of gains while preserving your integrity as a carrier of cultivation. The critical thing is knowing what may be conceded and what may not. Concedable: concrete interests, dignity for a time, nominal allegiance, some autonomy. Not concedable: the carrier itself — culture, language, spiritual tradition, education, the way subjectivity operates in daily life. Once those begin to be replaced, this is no longer trading gains for time. It is assimilation on an installment plan.
changes.after: The response is to concede at the level of gains while preserving your integrity as a subject of cultivation. The critical thing is knowing what may be conceded and what may not. Concedable: concrete interests, dignity for a time, nominal allegiance, some autonomy. Not concedable: the carrier itself — culture, language, spiritual tradition, education, the way subjectivity operates in daily life. Once those begin to be replaced, this is no longer trading gains for time. It is assimilation on an installment plan.
changes.reason: Restore 主体 and retain its distinction from the carrier discussed later in the same paragraph.

changes.before: Key people relocated, essential resources protected, the carriers of tradition — books, crafts, knowledge, transmission — moved somewhere safe first. This demands very clear judgment from leadership: choosing to withdraw while it still looks possible to make a stand preserves far more than withdrawing from a corner. Those who leave early can take the core with them; those who leave at the end often bring out only a remnant.
changes.after: Key people relocated, essential resources protected, the carriers of tradition — books, crafts, knowledge, transmission — moved somewhere safe first. This demands very clear judgment from leadership: choosing to withdraw while it still looks possible to make a stand often preserves far more than withdrawing from a corner. Those who leave early can take the core with them; those who leave at the end often bring out only a remnant.
changes.reason: Restore 往往 instead of asserting the comparison universally.

changes.before: Inward dispersal. The organization as a whole dissolves, but cultivation does not — it moves from the macroscopic and visible into the microscopic, individual, familial, and unseen. An occupier can destroy a government, a capital, an army. It has great difficulty destroying ten million dispersed individuals. As long as cultivation continues at the level of persons and households, the occupation cannot complete itself.
changes.after: Inward dispersal. The organization as a whole dissolves, but cultivation does not — it moves from the macroscopic and visible into the microscopic, individual, familial, and unseen. An occupier can destroy a government, a capital, an army. It has great difficulty destroying tens of millions of dispersed individuals. As long as cultivation continues at the level of persons and households, the occupation cannot complete itself.
changes.reason: Avoid turning 千万个 into the exact singular number ten million.

changes.before: Every person who keeps speaking their own language under occupation, every text passed hand to hand, every lesson taught in a private parlour, is cultivation in dispersed form.
changes.after: Every person who keeps speaking their own language under occupation, every text passed secretly from hand to hand, every lesson taught in a private parlour, is cultivation in dispersed form.
changes.reason: Restore secrecy as the mechanism of dispersed preservation.

changes.before: Four points here. First, allies must be structurally alike — ally with another suppressive structure on the logic that an enemy's enemy is a friend, and sooner or later that ally will act like what it is and destroy with its own hands what you preserved. Second, an ally must protect your subjectivity rather than liberate on your behalf; the firewall above applies inside alliances too, and not all aid is adequate aid. Third, an ally having stakes of its own is a healthy anchor, not a stain. Fourth, outward connection is not always available: sometimes there is no ally to find, and dispersal can only go inward — at greater cost, over longer time, depending more heavily on internal resilience.
changes.after: Four points here. First, allies must be structurally alike — ally with another suppressive structure on the logic that an enemy's enemy is a friend, and sooner or later that ally will act like what it is and destroy with its own hands what you preserved. Second, an ally must protect your subjectivity rather than liberate on your behalf; the firewall above applies inside alliances too, and not all aid is adequate aid. Third, an ally having stakes of its own is a healthy anchor, not a stain. Fourth, outward connection is no cure-all: sometimes there is no ally to find, and dispersal can only go inward — at greater cost, over longer time, depending more heavily on internal resilience.
changes.reason: Restore the broader limitation 不是万能的, before the example of unavailable allies.

changes.before: But stopping is only the first step. The second is returning to negotiation and maneuver — the collisions that caused the war have not been handled and will still be there, only now handled by other means.
changes.after: But stopping is only the first step. The second is returning to negotiation and maneuver — if the collisions that caused the war have not been handled, they will still be there, only now handled by other means.
changes.reason: Restore the conditional 如果 rather than assert all underlying collisions remain untreated.

changes.before: The structure works like this. To guard against the other side over a long standoff, you must come to resemble it in organization, institutions, narrative, and mobilization. They have a powerful mobilization apparatus, so you build one to match. They use a wartime narrative to hold their interior together, so you use one too. They suppress internal dissent to maintain unity, so you suppress yours to avoid "being divided." They treat people as executing units, so you do it for "efficiency."
changes.after: The structure works like this. To guard against the other side over a long standoff, you must increasingly come to resemble it in organization, institutions, narrative, and mobilization. They have a powerful mobilization apparatus, so you build one to match. They use a wartime narrative to hold their interior together, so you use one too, to avoid being outdone. They suppress internal dissent to maintain unity, so you suppress yours to avoid "being divided." They treat people as executing units, so you do it for "efficiency."
changes.reason: Restore the progressive resemblance and the specific motive for adopting the other side's narrative.

changes.before: And what Theorem Three requires under all three forms is a single sentence: let no state of the war harden into a permanent one, so that cultivation genuinely returns to its home ground afterward.
changes.after: And what Theorem Three requires under all three forms is a single sentence: let no state of the war harden into a long-term one, so that cultivation genuinely returns to its home ground afterward.
changes.reason: Restore 长期 without strengthening it to permanent.

unresolved_source_questions.finding: The temporary restriction of dissent is called potentially adequate in wartime, while ep05 requires questioners to be protected and allows no failure in its four layers. This needs an authorial boundary, not a translator-created exception.
Article 231 wording is the subject of the separate, sourced author-amendments proposal. No historical correction applied in English before approval.
The two-power standard is presented as a response during the 1898–1912 Anglo-German race; verify its 1889 adoption and distinguish older standard from later application.

metadata_changes.before: A victor's two obligations and the firewall against liberating on someone's behalf; why defeat is not losing and self-annihilation is never structurally adequate; and the hidden toxicity of stalemate — you never lost on the battlefield, but across the standoff you became their mirror.
metadata_changes.after: A victor's two obligations and the firewall against liberating on someone's behalf; why defeat is not losing and self-annihilation is never structurally adequate; and the most hidden toxicity in a balance of power — you never lost on the battlefield, but across the standoff you became their mirror.
metadata_changes.reason: Restore 均势 and its superlative rather than equate it with stalemate.
